### Import packages

```{r import-packages, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(tidyr)
library(ranger)    
library(pROC)     
library(knitr)
library(ggplot2)   
set.seed(1213) # same seed as LASSO
```

## 1. Load data

```{r load-data}
macro <- read_csv("../data/processed/fred_md_macro_clean_final.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
macro_fin <- read_csv("../data/processed/fred_md_macro_financial_clean_final.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

# Number of predictors (p) used to set mtry later
p_macro <- ncol(macro) - 2  # excludes sasdate and USREC
p_macro_fin <- ncol(macro_fin) - 2
c(p_macro = p_macro, p_macro_fin = p_macro_fin)
```

## 2. Target construction

Construct Y_3, Y_6 and Y_12 columns for 3, 6 and 12 month horizons.

```{r target-construction}

# Construct Y_3, Y_6, Y_12 
create_targets <- function(df) {
  df <- df %>%
    arrange(sasdate)
  for (h in c(3, 6, 12)) {
    future_recession <- sapply(
      seq_len(nrow(df)),
      function(i) {
        future_rows <- (i + 1):(i + h)
        # Exclude observations without complete future data
        if (max(future_rows) > nrow(df)) {
          return(NA_integer_)
        }
        future_values <- df$USREC[future_rows]
        # Handle missing recession indicators
        if (any(is.na(future_values))) {
          return(NA_integer_)
        }

        # 1 if any future month is recessionary
        as.integer(any(future_values == 1))
      }
    )
    df[[paste0("Y_", h)]] <- future_recession
  }
  return(df)
}


macro <- create_targets(macro)
macro_fin <- create_targets(macro_fin)

# logic check using 2008 recession as example
macro %>%
  select(sasdate, USREC, Y_3, Y_6, Y_12) %>%
  filter(
    sasdate >= as.Date("2007-01-01"),
    sasdate <= as.Date("2008-06-01")
  ) %>%
  print(n = Inf)
```

## 3. Train-Test Split

Rows before 1986-01-01 form the training set, and rows from 1986-01-01 onwards form the test set.

```{r train-test-split}
test_start <- as.Date("1986-01-01")

# Label training and testing periods
macro <- macro %>% 
  mutate(sample = if_else(sasdate < test_start, "train", "test"))

macro_fin <- macro_fin %>% 
  mutate(sample = if_else(sasdate < test_start, "train", "test"))

# Check the split
macro %>%
  group_by(sample) %>%
  summarise(start_date = min(sasdate),
            end_date = max(sasdate),
            observations = n(),
            recession_months = sum(USREC == 1),
            .groups = "drop")

macro_fin %>%
  group_by(sample) %>%
  summarise(start_date = min(sasdate), 
            end_date = max(sasdate), 
            observations = n(), 
            recession_months = sum(USREC == 1), 
            .groups = "drop")
```

## 4. Random Forest and Bagging

Here, we use an expanding window (same as other models). At each forecast date, the model is trained on all rows whose target period has already ended, then predict using that month's indicators. 

We try both Random Forest and Bagging. Bagging is a random forest with `mtry = p`. We run our first pass with 500 trees, `mtry = floor(sqrt(p))` for RF, with no tuning.

```{r forecast-rf-function}
forecast_rf <- function(df, horizon, model_type = c("RF", "Bagging"), mtry = NULL,
                        num_trees = 500, refit_every = 1,
                        test_start = as.Date("1986-01-01")) {
  model_type <- match.arg(model_type)  # check that model type is one of the 2 options
  target <- paste0("Y_", horizon)

  # exclude non-predictor columns
  predictor_cols <- setdiff(names(df), c("sasdate", "USREC", "Y_3", "Y_6", "Y_12", "sample"))
  p <- length(predictor_cols)
  if (is.null(mtry)) mtry <- if (model_type == "RF") floor(sqrt(p)) else p   

  df <- df %>% arrange(sasdate)

  # start from beginning of test set and drop test observations with unknown outcomes
  test_indices <- which(df$sasdate >= test_start & !is.na(df[[target]]))
  results <- vector("list", length(test_indices))
  model <- NULL

  for (j in seq_along(test_indices)) {
    i <- test_indices[j]

    # re-fit on an expanding window every 1 month
    if ((j - 1) %% refit_every == 0) {
      # build training set using expanding window 
      train_data <- df[seq_len(i - horizon - 1), , drop = FALSE] %>%
        filter(!is.na(.data[[target]]))

      model <- ranger(
        x = train_data[, predictor_cols],
        y = factor(train_data[[target]], levels = c(0, 1)),
        num.trees = num_trees,
        mtry = mtry,
        probability = TRUE  # output recession probabilities instead of binary values
      )
    }

    # predict current test month using current month's indicators
    prob <- predict(model, df[i, predictor_cols])$predictions[, "1"]

    # store results
    results[[j]] <- data.frame(
      sasdate = df$sasdate[i],
      horizon = horizon,
      actual = df[[target]][i],
      predicted_prob = prob
    )
  }
  bind_rows(results)
}
```

```{r rf-forecasts}
datasets <- list(Macro = macro, Macro_Financial = macro_fin)
horizons <- c(3, 6, 12)
model_types <- c("RF", "Bagging")

rf_file <- "../data/results/rf_forecasts.rds"

# load saved forecasts if exists, if not run every combination (delete the file to force a re-run)
if (file.exists(rf_file)) {
  rf_forecast_results <- readRDS(rf_file)
} else {
  all_forecasts <- list()

  for (dataset_name in names(datasets)) {
    for (h in horizons) {
      for (model_type in model_types) {
        cat("Running:", dataset_name, h, model_type, "\n")
        result <- forecast_rf(
          df = datasets[[dataset_name]],
          horizon = h,
          model_type = model_type
        )
        result$dataset <- dataset_name
        result$model <- model_type
        all_forecasts[[paste(dataset_name, h, model_type, sep = "_")]] <- result
      }
    }
  }

  # combine and save results
  rf_forecast_results <- bind_rows(all_forecasts)
  dir.create(dirname(rf_file), showWarnings = FALSE)
  saveRDS(rf_forecast_results, rf_file)
}

head(rf_forecast_results)
```

```{r rf-forecast-check}
# verify that all 12 configurations ran successfully
rf_forecast_results %>%
  group_by(dataset, horizon, model) %>%
  summarise(n_forecasts  = n(),
            unique_dates = n_distinct(sasdate),
            .groups = "drop")
```

```{r rf-extreme-predictions}
# check months where model is very confident of a recession, and whether they were correct
rf_forecast_results %>%
  filter(predicted_prob > 0.9) %>%
  group_by(dataset, horizon, model) %>%
  summarise(
    n_extreme = n(),
    correct   = sum(actual == 1),
    incorrect = sum(actual == 0),
    false_positive_dates = paste(as.character(sasdate[actual == 0]), collapse = ", "),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

## 5. Evaluation

### 5.1 Forecast metrics

The same metrics are used across all models, so that the results are directly comparable. AUC is the main metric. F1 score and balanced accuracy use a 0.5 threshold.

```{r rf-evaluate}
evaluate_forecasts <- function(df, threshold = 0.5) {
  actual <- df$actual
  prob <- df$predicted_prob

  # convert probabilities into binary predictions
  predicted <- as.integer(prob >= threshold)

  # confusion matrix components
  TP <- sum(predicted == 1 & actual == 1)
  TN <- sum(predicted == 0 & actual == 0)
  FP <- sum(predicted == 1 & actual == 0)
  FN <- sum(predicted == 0 & actual == 1)

  # classification metrics
  precision <- ifelse(TP + FP == 0, 0, TP / (TP + FP))
  recall <- ifelse(TP + FN == 0, NA_real_, TP / (TP + FN))
  specificity <- ifelse(TN + FP == 0, NA_real_, TN / (TN + FP))
  f1 <- ifelse(precision + recall == 0, 0, 2 * precision * recall / (precision + recall))
  balanced_accuracy <- (recall + specificity) / 2

  # probability-based evaluation
  brier <- mean((actual - prob)^2)

  # ROC-AUC
  auc_value <- as.numeric(auc(roc(actual, prob, quiet = TRUE)))
  data.frame(AUC = auc_value, F1 = f1, Balanced_Accuracy = balanced_accuracy, Brier = brier)
}

rf_evaluation_results <- rf_forecast_results %>%
  group_by(dataset, horizon, model) %>%
  group_modify(~ evaluate_forecasts(.x)) %>%
  ungroup()

print(rf_evaluation_results, n = Inf)
```

### 5.2 Macro vs Macro + Financial

We find the gain from adding financial variables for each horizon and model. We do this by differencing the AUC, F1 scores, Balanced Accuracy, and Brier scores for macro only vs macro + financial. 
For each gain / improvement metric, a positive value means financial variables help.

```{r rf-financial-comparison}
rf_financial_comparison <- rf_evaluation_results %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = dataset,
              values_from = c(AUC, F1, Balanced_Accuracy, Brier)) %>%
  mutate(
    AUC_gain = AUC_Macro_Financial - AUC_Macro,
    F1_gain = F1_Macro_Financial - F1_Macro,
    Balanced_Accuracy_gain = Balanced_Accuracy_Macro_Financial - Balanced_Accuracy_Macro,
    Brier_improvement = Brier_Macro - Brier_Macro_Financial # Brier is flipped because lower is better
  ) %>%
  select(horizon, model, AUC_gain, F1_gain, Balanced_Accuracy_gain, Brier_improvement) %>%
  arrange(model, horizon)

print(rf_financial_comparison, n = Inf)
```

### 5.3 Check if AUC gain is real (block bootstrap)

To check whether the AUC gain from adding financial variables is real or due to chance, we rebuild the test period 1,000 times by randomly drawing 24-month chunks of test months, and recompute the gain each time. We use chunks rather than single months so that each recession’s months stay together since they are correlated. Both models are scored on the same months each time. If the 95% confidence interval lies entirely above 0, we can conclude that adding financial variables significantly improves AUC at that horizon.

```{r rf-auc-bootstrap, cache=TRUE}
block_bootstrap_auc_gain <- function(actual, prob_macro, prob_fin,
                                     block_length = 24, n_boot = 1000) {
  n <- length(actual)
  n_blocks <- ceiling(n / block_length)

  gains <- replicate(n_boot, {
    starts <- sample(1:(n - block_length + 1), n_blocks, replace = TRUE)
    idx <- unlist(lapply(starts, function(s) s:(s + block_length - 1)))[1:n]
    y <- actual[idx]
    if (length(unique(y)) < 2) return(NA_real_)   # resample with no recession: skip
    as.numeric(auc(y, prob_fin[idx], quiet = TRUE)) -
      as.numeric(auc(y, prob_macro[idx], quiet = TRUE))
  })

  data.frame(
    AUC_gain = as.numeric(auc(actual, prob_fin, quiet = TRUE)) -
               as.numeric(auc(actual, prob_macro, quiet = TRUE)),
    CI_lower = quantile(gains, 0.025, na.rm = TRUE),
    CI_upper = quantile(gains, 0.975, na.rm = TRUE),
    valid_resamples = sum(!is.na(gains))
  )
}

set.seed(1213)
auc_gain_ci <- rf_forecast_results %>%
  select(sasdate, horizon, model, dataset, actual, predicted_prob) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = dataset, values_from = predicted_prob) %>%
  arrange(sasdate) %>%
  group_by(horizon, model) %>%
  group_modify(~ block_bootstrap_auc_gain(.x$actual, .x$Macro, .x$Macro_Financial)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(significant = CI_lower > 0 | CI_upper < 0) %>%
  arrange(model, horizon)

print(auc_gain_ci, n = Inf)
```

### 5.4 RF vs Bagging

Positive values in the difference means RF beats bagging. If bagging wins on Macro + Financial but not on Macro, a dominant financial predictor is likely driving the result.

```{r rf-vs-bagging}
rf_vs_bagging <- rf_evaluation_results %>%
  select(dataset, horizon, model, AUC) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = model, values_from = AUC) %>%
  mutate(RF_minus_Bagging = RF - Bagging) %>%
  arrange(dataset, horizon)

print(rf_vs_bagging, n = Inf)
```

### 5.5 Recession-by-recession check

For exploratory purposes.

```{r rf-recession-episodes}
# Recession start dates in the test period
test_recessions <- macro %>%
  arrange(sasdate) %>%
  filter(USREC == 1, lag(USREC, default = 0) == 0, sasdate >= test_start) %>%
  pull(sasdate)

# Months from date a to date b
month_diff <- function(a, b) {
  (as.POSIXlt(b)$year - as.POSIXlt(a)$year) * 12 + (as.POSIXlt(b)$mon - as.POSIXlt(a)$mon)
}

threshold <- 0.5

# For each recession: forecasts made in the h months before it started
recession_signals <- rf_forecast_results %>%
  crossing(recession_start = test_recessions) %>%
  mutate(months_before = month_diff(sasdate, recession_start)) %>%
  filter(months_before >= 1, months_before <= horizon) %>%
  group_by(dataset, horizon, model, recession_start) %>%
  summarise(
    max_prob = max(predicted_prob),
    flagged = any(predicted_prob >= threshold),
    earliest_warning_months = if (any(predicted_prob >= threshold))
      max(months_before[predicted_prob >= threshold]) else NA_real_,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

print(recession_signals, n = Inf)

# Summary: recessions flagged in advance (out of 4) and false-alarm months
recession_summary <- recession_signals %>%
  group_by(dataset, horizon, model) %>%
  summarise(recessions_flagged = sum(flagged),
            total_recessions = n(),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  left_join(
    rf_forecast_results %>%
      group_by(dataset, horizon, model) %>%
      summarise(false_alarm_months = sum(predicted_prob >= threshold & actual == 0),
                .groups = "drop"),
    by = c("dataset", "horizon", "model")
  ) %>%
  arrange(model, dataset, horizon)

print(recession_summary, n = Inf)
```

### 5.6 ROC curves

```{r rf-roc-curves, fig.width=10, fig.height=4}
roc_data <- rf_forecast_results %>%
  filter(model == "RF") %>%
  group_by(dataset, horizon) %>%
  group_modify(~ {
    r <- roc(.x$actual, .x$predicted_prob, quiet = TRUE)
    tibble(fpr = 1 - r$specificities,
           tpr = r$sensitivities,
           auc = as.numeric(auc(r)))
  }) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  arrange(dataset, horizon, fpr, tpr)

# AUC labels for each panel
auc_labels <- roc_data %>%
  distinct(dataset, horizon, auc) %>%
  mutate(label = sprintf("%s: AUC = %.2f",
                         if_else(dataset == "Macro", "Macro", "Macro + Financial"), auc))

ggplot(roc_data, aes(x = fpr, y = tpr, colour = dataset)) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey60") +
  geom_step(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_text(data = auc_labels,
            aes(x = 0.98, y = if_else(dataset == "Macro", 0.08, 0.16), label = label),
            hjust = 1, size = 3, show.legend = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~ horizon, labeller = labeller(horizon = function(h) paste0(h, "-month horizon"))) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(Macro = "#7A7A7A", Macro_Financial = "#1F5FA8"),
                      labels = c(Macro = "Macro only", Macro_Financial = "Macro + Financial")) +
  coord_equal() +
  labs(title = "Random forest ROC curves, out-of-sample 1986 onwards",
       x = "False positive rate (false alarms)", y = "True positive rate (recessions caught)",
       colour = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(legend.position = "top", panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
```

## 6. Variable Importance

Permutation importance from RF model fitted on Macro + Financial data for all months with a known outcome. This is for interpretation only. It tells us which predictors the RF relies on most at each horizon.

```{r var-importance}
set.seed(1213)
fin_vars <- setdiff(names(macro_fin), names(macro))   # the 25 financial series
predictor_cols <- setdiff(names(macro_fin), c("sasdate", "USREC", "Y_3", "Y_6", "Y_12", "sample"))

importance_results <- bind_rows(lapply(c(3, 6, 12), function(h) {
  target <- paste0("Y_", h)
  d <- macro_fin %>% filter(!is.na(.data[[target]]))
  fit <- ranger(
    x = d[, predictor_cols],
    y = factor(d[[target]], levels = c(0, 1)),
    num.trees = 500,
    mtry = floor(sqrt(length(predictor_cols))),
    probability = TRUE,
    importance = "permutation"
  )
  tibble(horizon = h,
         variable = names(fit$variable.importance),
         importance = fit$variable.importance)
})) %>%
  mutate(group = if_else(variable %in% fin_vars, "Financial", "Macro"))

# Top 10 predictors per horizon
importance_results %>%
  group_by(horizon) %>%
  slice_max(importance, n = 10) %>%
  mutate(rank = row_number()) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  print(n = Inf)

# Share of total importance from financial vs macro predictors
importance_results %>%
  mutate(importance = pmax(importance, 0)) %>%
  group_by(horizon, group) %>%
  summarise(total = sum(importance), .groups = "drop_last") %>%
  mutate(share = total / sum(total)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(-total) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = group, values_from = share)
```


## 7. Tuning mtry

Validation uses only pre-1986 data: forecasts for 1981–85 from an expanding window that starts in 1962, with targets rebuilt on the truncated data so no post-1985 outcome is used. The 1981–82 recession falls in this block.

```{r rf-tune-mtry, cache=TRUE}
val_start <- as.Date("1981-01-01")

# Validation data: pre-1986 months only, with targets rebuilt so no post-1985 outcome is used
make_val_data <- function(df) {
  df %>%
    filter(sasdate < test_start) %>%
    select(-Y_3, -Y_6, -Y_12) %>%
    create_targets()
}

# Candidate mtry values between sqrt(p) and p
mtry_grid <- function(p) unique(c(floor(sqrt(p)), floor(2 * sqrt(p)), floor(p / 3), floor(p / 2), p))

set.seed(1213)
tuning_results <- list()

for (dataset_name in names(datasets)) {
  val_df <- make_val_data(datasets[[dataset_name]])
  p <- length(setdiff(names(val_df), c("sasdate", "USREC", "Y_3", "Y_6", "Y_12", "sample")))

  for (h in horizons) {
    for (m in mtry_grid(p)) {
      f <- forecast_rf(val_df, h, "RF", mtry = m, refit_every = 12, test_start = val_start)
      tuning_results[[paste(dataset_name, h, m, sep = "_")]] <- tibble(
        dataset = dataset_name, horizon = h, mtry = m,
        val_AUC = as.numeric(auc(f$actual, f$predicted_prob, quiet = TRUE))
      )
    }
  }
}

tuning_results <- bind_rows(tuning_results)
print(tuning_results, n = Inf)

# Best mtry for each dataset x horizon
best_mtry <- tuning_results %>%
  group_by(dataset, horizon) %>%
  slice_max(val_AUC, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  ungroup()
best_mtry
```
